spec_facts.statement: ML-KEM represents polynomials in R_q as length-256 arrays of coefficients over Z_q, with f[ i ] equal to the i-th coefficient f_i for i in {0,...,255}.

evidence_references.excerpt: An element f of R_q is a polynomial f = f_0 + f_1 X + ⋯ + f_255 X^255 ∈ R_q and will be represented in pseudocode by the array (f_0, f_1, …, f_255) ∈ Z_q^256... The i-th entry of the array f will thus contain the i-th coefficient of the polynomial f (i.e., f[i] = f_i).
evidence_references.supports_claim: R_q polynomials are represented as length-256 coefficient arrays over Z_q, with direct index-to-coefficient correspondence.

spec_facts.statement: The NTT representation T_q is also represented in pseudocode as a length-256 array of coefficients modulo q, with paired coordinates mapping as g[2i] = ĝ_{i,0} and g[2i+1] = ĝ_{i,1} for i in {0,...,127}.
spec_facts.verification_relevance: candidate algorithm-to-code trace item for representing polynomial addition in either R_q or T_q arrays.

evidence_references.excerpt: An element (sometimes called “NTT representation”) ĝ of T_q is a tuple of 128 polynomials... Such an algebraic object will be represented in pseudocode by the array (...) ∈ Z_q^256. Overloading notation, the array in (2.7) will also be denoted by ĝ. In this case, the mapping between array entries and coefficients is ĝ[2i] = ĝ_{i,0} and ĝ[2i + 1] = ĝ_{i,1} for i ∈ {0, 1, … , 127}.
evidence_references.supports_claim: T_q elements are encoded as length-256 coefficient arrays with pairwise coordinate mapping.

spec_facts.statement: Arithmetic on arrays of integers modulo m is performed coordinate-wise: if Z ← a⋅X or W ← X+Y, then Z[i] = a⋅X[i] and W[i] = X[i] + Y[i] for all i, with modular reduction implicit in Z_m.

functions.name: mlk_poly_add
functions.role: In-place polynomial addition over coefficient arrays; updates the first operand accumulator `r` by adding corresponding coefficients from `b`.
outputs: No return value; mutates r->coeffs in place
preconditions_or_contracts: `r` and `b` must be memory-no-alias fresh objects per `memory_no_alias(r, sizeof(mlk_poly))` and `memory_no_alias(b, sizeof(mlk_poly))`.
For every coefficient index `k0` in [0, MLKEM_N), `(int32_t) r->coeffs[k0] + b->coeffs[k0] <= INT16_MAX`.
For every coefficient index `k1` in [0, MLKEM_N), `(int32_t) r->coeffs[k1] + b->coeffs[k1] >= INT16_MIN`.
postconditions_or_contracts: For every coefficient index `k` in [0, MLKEM_N), `r->coeffs[k] == old(*r).coeffs[k] + b->coeffs[k]`.
